Input null of the tumour mode: depth t null and allelic rho

Source: R/clones_tumour.R
tumour_null_fit.Rd

The depth Student-t null (fit_depth_null(), completed by class) and the beta-binomial rho (fit_allelic_null() on the arm rows with votes) that caller_tumour() uses for discovery, assignment and per-cell confirmation, fitted on the null rows (null_region and eligible) of a set of cells:

  • "flagged": the cells with null_cell TRUE (the flat column of the cell metadata, or given null cells), whenever there is one and select is FALSE;

  • "selected": otherwise, the cells without a call on the null rows, as select_null_cells() finds them (chromosome and arm rows, the tumour state set, n_iter iterations from all cells minus exclude and minus the cells of its windowed allele guard, params$null_win_guard): the cells kept by both of its last two iterations. They are used when there are at least min_cells of them and the last iteration is stable (Jaccard index of the sets it started from and ended with >= min_jaccard). In a tumour sample with normal cells that the null rows separate from the tumour, these are mostly the normal cells; tumour cells whose events all lie outside the null rows or are too weak to call per cell pass as well; without such cells the selection usually does not settle;

  • "all": otherwise all cells (no stable selection). The fit then absorbs the tumour's events on the null rows (inflated rho, heavy depth tails), as every tumour-mode run without flagged cells did before.

Usage

tumour_null_fit(
  long,
  params = caller_defaults(),
  exclude = NULL,
  select = FALSE,
  n_iter = 5,
  min_cells = 5,
  min_jaccard = 0.7,
  max_share = 2/3
)

Arguments

long

features long table (cell_features() long: cell, region, class, sd_class, chrom, stratum, z, sd_null, nA, n_hap, null_region, eligible, null_cell)

params

caller_defaults()

exclude

cells never selected (e.g. multiplets)

select

TRUE: select the cells even when some are flagged

n_iter

iterations of the selection (>= 2)

min_cells

minimal number of selected cells

min_jaccard

minimal Jaccard index of the selection's last iteration

max_share

share of the candidate cells above which a selected set gets a caution (2 / 3); the fit is not changed

Value

NULL without null rows (of the flagged cells); else list(tpar, rho, source = "flagged" / "selected" / "all", null_cells (the cells fitted), selection (the select_null_cells() log; NULL for flagged cells), share (selected cells / candidate cells; NA for flagged cells), caution (NULL, or one line when a selected set holds more than max_share of the candidates), note (one line for the run notes))

Details

A fit on all cells is wrong whenever tumour cells carry events on the null rows: rho and the t tails take up the events, which weakens assignment and per-cell confirmation. Flagged copy-number-normal cells (e.g. from a matched assay) remain the better null: a stable selection does not show that the selected cells are copy-number neutral. In a tumour in which almost every cell carries the same clonal events on the null rows, the selection fits its null to those events and then keeps most of the cells. When it keeps more than max_share of the candidate cells (all cells minus exclude, guarded cells included), the result carries a caution and the note says so; call_scn() then warns. The note also gives the rho of all cells next to the fitted one: a selected null whose rho is close to the all-cell rho is a set of tumour cells that carry the same events.
